answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity’s action vector is hashed per epoch; continuity requires the next epoch’s vector to fall within a small distance of the prior one, checked at a bridge node that compares incoming records before admitting them to the shared inlet of active agents. A sybil must operate every clone across epochs to keep fingerprints coherent, so its cost scales linearly with fleet size and detection lag shrinks. Divergent clones form a plume of flagged traces that bars admission.
